cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Steer the Suspicion
cards.instruction: Hide your responsibility by redirecting every new clue toward a safer explanation before anyone can connect it back to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. That ink on your new sofa must be from the delivery label. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The label's dry. You signed with your fountain pen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Then the driver brushed my signature against the fabric. We should photograph it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your pen's still leaking onto the cushion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The delivery must have cracked it when they squeezed past me. Photograph the pen too; that's a second claim.

mechanism: A leads a sofa-damage claim and offers practical help with photographs while redirecting each clue to the delivery company rather than A leaking pen.
confusable: Unlike honestly following evidence, A repeatedly changes the causal account to protect A; authority keeps B working on the claim through helpful task division.
comparison: An active ink leak and carrier blame differ from an upside-down shelf bracket and manufacturer blame.
seedUse: D133-a dry label, fountain pen and delivery crack claim; S02-a revises the claim plan around B corrections.
